title: Blanket wash
description: Six sheets pulled from the house press while the blanket was washed with solvent between runs. One plate, a view of the Panke from the loading bay. Sheet 1 carries full ink density; each later sheet holds less, until only the register marks and a grey trace remain. Read in the order they were pulled.

title: Ink limit
description: The house control strip, enlarged to sheet size and printed nine times as a 1-bit file at 60 lpi. Total ink coverage rises from 200 to 400 per cent in steps of 25. Dot gain is read with the house densitometer and noted on each sheet; from 325 per cent upwards the paper cockles. Read in ascending order.

title: No negative
medium: Generated, offset on 80 gsm newsprint, 60 lpi
description: Eight images generated from one prompt: a halftone negative on a light table. No negative exists; the file goes straight to plate. Printed offset on 80 gsm newsprint at 60 lpi, so the only screen in the chain is the one on the paper. Sheets in generation order, seed numbers in the lower margin.

title: Corniche, noon
medium: Riso, fluorescent orange and blue, 60 lpi
description: Five 35 mm frames of the Corniche at Aïn Diab, Casablanca, exposed between 11:40 and 12:20. Each frame is split at a threshold: fluorescent orange for surfaces in direct sun, blue for shadow. Two drums, no grey; where the layers meet, the feed sets the gap. Sheets follow the time of exposure; the shadow layer shortens from sheet to sheet.

title: Halation
description: Harbour lamps on the Halifax waterfront, 35 mm, exposures from 1 to 30 seconds. Each negative was enlarged onto 60 lpi halftone film at sheet size and contact printed on gelatin silver paper. At the lamp cores the dots close into halos; the negative's halation becomes dot size. Six sheets, ordered by exposure time.

title: Second drum
medium: Riso, black and medium blue, 60 lpi
description: Two riso drums. Black carries the Third Mainland Bridge, photographed from a moving bus; medium blue carries the lagoon beneath it. The second pass drifts as the feed varies. Six sheets sorted by the measured shift between the two colours, from 0 to 3 mm. Screened at 60 lpi before separation.

title: Warp count
description: Jacquard cloth samples from a Łódź mill archive, photographed at 1:1 and screened to 60 lpi positives. Five copper plates, one per sample, at warp densities from 12 to 40 threads per centimetre. From sheet 3 onwards the weave and the screen ruling beat against each other. Read from coarse to fine.

title: Sixty lines
medium: Generated, offset on 45 gsm newsprint, 60 lpi
description: Five images generated from a prompt for a sixty-line screen: blinds, fences, ploughed fields, ruled paper. Printed offset at 60 lpi on 45 gsm newsprint. The lines depicted and the screen ruling coincide or beat against each other. Sheets ordered from coarse to fine, by the number of lines depicted.

title: Spoilage
description: Seven makeready sheets from the first year of the press hall. Each sheet was fed through the press repeatedly while successive jobs were set up: posters, an edition, a test form. Register marks and colour bars accumulate in the margins. The date of each pass is written in pencil. Read in press-log order.

title: Paper white
medium: Gelatin silver, fibre paper, 60 lpi film
description: Plaster walls and snow banks in Kanazawa, photographed in overcast light. Negatives screened to 60 lpi film and printed on fibre paper. Where the subject is white, no dot falls and the paper stays unexposed. Eight sheets ordered by the share of paper left white, from 12 to 90 per cent.

title: Vine black
description: One 60 lpi screen of Ogbete market in Enugu after closing. Four pulls in vine black on 300 gsm rag, each with more squeegee pressure than the last. On sheet 1 the dots stand apart; on sheet 4 they have joined and the stalls are a single dark field. Read 1 to 4.

title: Paraná, six rolls
medium: Contact sheet, 35 mm, gelatin silver RC
description: Six rolls of 35 mm exposed from a grain barge between Rosario and San Lorenzo over one day. Each sheet is one roll, contact printed uncut on RC paper: 36 frames with their edge numbers, leader and tail. Nothing is enlarged or selected. Sheets in the order the rolls were loaded, 1 to 6.
